r.b: Q: What is the attendance capacity for this YCS?

Q: How many Rounds will the Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series have?

r: The total number of Duelists in each of the Main Events, Advanced and Genesys, will determine the number of Rounds that are played in that specific Main Event.

r.b: Q: How many Duelists will advance to Day 2?

r: If there are 256 or fewer Duelists registered for one of the Main Events, Advanced or Genesys, then the Top 64 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 15 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2 for that specific Main Event.
If there are 257 – 512 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 64 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 18 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 513 – 1024 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 128 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 18 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 1025 – 2048 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 256 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 21 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 2049 or more Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 256 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 21 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.

r.b: Q: What cards are legal for play?

r: Please check the “Products” page online at https://www.yugioh‐card.com/en/products/ for the most current legality dates of Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME product releases, prior to preparing your Deck for the event.
Cards that have been altered from their original appearance with surface decoration may be used for play
only if the alterations do not obscure any portion of the card text, make the illustration difficult to recognize, or make the card distinguishable from other cards in the Deck while it is face-down.
If a card’s surface decoration renders the card unrecognizable at first glance, then the card is not allowed for tournament play.

The Head Judge of the event has final arbitration on whether or not altered cards may be used at the tournament. Duelists are responsible for determining whether or not their altered cards are acceptable for use before the start of the tournament.

r: This will be a two-day Remote Duel tournament using the Genesys 100 Points cap for Deck-building Constructed Decks in the Swiss format:
Best 2 out of 3 Matches
Swiss Rounds followed by a Single-Elimination Playoff Top Cut. Rounds are dependent on the total number of Duelists at the time registration closes.

Remote Duel is Sanctioned Organized Play hosted in a virtual environment, run on designated Discord servers. To participate, TCG Duelists will need a webcam, smartphone or tablet to display their field to their opponent. These events are perfect for Duelists that want to play from the comfort of their homes or are unable to travel to in-person YCS events!

r.b: You can find more details on Remote Duel on our website:

r: https://www.yugioh-card.com/en/remoteduel/index.html.

Prior to registering for events, you should read the Remote Duel Best Practices Guide as it contains information you will need to compete: https://www.yugioh-card.com/en/downloads/remoteduel/EN_Remote_Duel_Best_Practice_Guide_V_1_2.pdf
You are responsible for a stable internet connection and a working Remote Duel setup in order to participate in a Remote Duel event.
If you lose your video feed, have excessively lagging or frozen video, or otherwise disconnect from a Duel in progress, you will receive a Game Loss.
Please be mindful of background noise around your Remote Duel setup, so you and your opponent can hear each other clearly.

r.b: Q: How many Duelists will advance to Day 2?

r: The number of Duelist that return for Day 2 will be based on actual registered Duelists plus all VIPS. (late entries will not be considered)
If there are 32 or fewer Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 8 Duelists will advance to Day 2.
If there are 33 – 64 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 16 Duelists or Duelists with a minimum of 15 points, whichever is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 65 – 128 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 32 Duelists or Duelists with a minimum of 15 points, whichever is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 129 – 256 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 64 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 15 points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 257 – 512 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 128 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 18 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 513 – 1024 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 128 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 18 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 1025 – 2048 Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 256 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 21 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 2049 or more Duelists registered for the YCS, then the Top 256 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 21 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.

For those joining our events for the first time, obtaining a CARD GAME ID is as easy as downloading the NEURON app. Once downloaded follow the steps below:

This CARD GAME ID will be used when registering for any Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG Sanctioned events which includes our Tier 1 Local Events, Tier 2 Regional Qualifiers, Dragon Duels and OTS Championships, Tier 3 YCS, Latin America National and WCQ events, and even Tier 4 World Championship.
Once you have a CARD GAME ID, we strongly encourage you to create a KONAMI ID and link the two accounts.

A KONAMI ID can be used across various online services provided by the KONAMI Group. Registration is free of charge and can be completed through the “New Registration” option on the My KONAMI website (https://my.konami.net) or directly through the NEURON app.

The most common uses of a KONAMI ID for Duelists include Yu-Gi-Oh! MASTER DUEL, Yu-Gi-Oh! DUEL LINKS, and Yu-Gi-Oh! NEURON. Linking your CARD GAME ID to a KONAMI ID helps ensure that your account information is properly associated with your Organized Play participation and allows you to access additional KONAMI services using a single account.

r.b: Q: How do I find my table during the Genesys Remote Duel YCS?

r: Each Round, pairings will be posted in a channel named

in the Remote Duel YCS Discord server. The pairings will be posted as a series of images. The images are the pairings for the Round, sorted by Duelists’ Last Name. Find your name on the Pairings channel to see the table you are assigned for the Round.

Alternatively, the same channel will also have a QR code posted to the Online Pairings website. For this website, you will enter your CARD GAME ID and the Online Pairings website will tell you what Table you are assigned for the Round. If you are not sure what your CARD GAME ID is, you can find it next to your name on the images of the pairings list and then use it for future Rounds.

Regardless of whether you find your assigned table through the pairings images or the Online Pairings website, once you have found your assigned table for the Round, you will be able to find it in the list of voice channels. and join that for your match.
